anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly: Application-level queries or transaction patterns demand more data processing, scanning, and logging than the business case requires.
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly: The optimizer relies on stale or incomplete statistics, causing systematic cardinality errors and sub-optimal execution plans.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly: Downstream replicas cannot ingest or apply primary log records fast enough, creating widening replication lag and retained log segments.

When these three root causes coincide, the database experiences an amplified feedback loop of stress: poorly written or chatty application logic generates heavyweight scans and bloated transactions; stale statistics mislead the optimizer into choosing even more I/O-intensive plans, further inflating CPU, memory, and log volume; the surge of redo and larger result sets saturates the replication pipeline, causing log-position gaps, replica staleness, and prolonged retention of primary log files. End-users see erratic and long-tail response times, timeouts, and inconsistent read results between primary and replicas, while administrators observe ballooning disk usage from un-recycled logs, frequent plan recompilations, and replica apply backlogs.

Causally, excessive scans and updates from the workload anomaly quickly invalidate existing statistics, yet high data-change velocity may still not trigger or complete automatic statistics refreshes, locking the optimizer into bad estimates. The resulting mis-estimated plans magnify resource consumption and redo generation, accelerating the growth of the transaction log. The swollen log stream overwhelms replication bandwidth or apply throughput, and the resulting lag prevents log truncation on the primary, further aggravating I/O pressure. Meanwhile, replicas starved of up-to-date data can no longer serve read traffic effectively, pushing more load back to the primary and deepening contention. Each anomaly thus reinforces the others, producing a compound performance and availability degradation that is far more severe than any individual issue in isolation.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for more data from a source/replica connection before aborting the read.
entry.trigger_condition: A replica waits longer than replica_net_timeout for more data from the source connection.
entry.workload_impact: The replication network read is aborted and the replica considers the connection interrupted.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL replication system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
